main_text.p: in Italiam transsmisit, ubi in lapicidinas dati fuere. Legatis domum reversis, & per eos senatus Romani voluntate cognita, Ætoli in arma rursum versi Naupacto contra obsidionem, quam expectabant, prospexêre. Sed Acilius non Naupactum, sed Lamiam, præter eorum expectationem invasit, eaqué brevi tempore expugnata, Amphissa Locridis, quæ præsidio Ætolorum tenebatur, armis ab eodem petita. Cujus oppugnationi intervenit novus consul L. Scipio, Acilii successor, legato utens fratre Africano. Is accepto exercitu in cæpto oppugnationis progressus, nequicquam Atheniensibus cum Africano intercedentibus, non alias pacis conditiones admittere voluit, quàm quas senati [illegible, ~3 letters] Romæ tulerat. Verum connitentibus A rursum iisdem semestres induciæ dem Ætolis concessæ, obsidioque Amphissæ soluta. His induciis fluentibus bellum in Asiam translatum, atque ut terrâ marique gestum, variante interdum fortunâ, ac demum cunctis viribus de rerum summâ certatum, victusque fractusque Antiochus, ac trans Taurū montem submotus, paxque petentibus S ta. Interim Romæ quoque in curiâ per legatos Ætolorum instaurata rursum actio de pace, sed fine fructu. Nam etiam

page.notes: Right-margin marks beside the lines "admittere", "Verum" to "rursum", "dem Ætolis" and "ta" are short and too faint to read; they are shown only as approximate placeholders. Doubtful readings: "transsmisit" (long s rendered as f in the scan), "senati" (end of line faint), "connitentibus" (partly cut at the edge), "Amphissæ" and "Taurū" (abbreviation mark uncertain). The signature "s 5" is read from the faint foot mark. Show-through from the reverse page appears at the left margin and is not transcribed.
